text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure, or hypertension, is diagnosed when readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
Blood pressure measurements use two numbers: the top number (systolic) and the bottom number (diastolic).

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg top and less than 80 mm Hg bottom.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg top and less than 80 mm Hg bottom.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg top or 80–89 mm Hg bottom.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher top, or 90 mm Hg or higher bottom.
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg top and/or higher than 120 mm Hg bottom.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more details on the American Heart Association Guidelines or check the CDC High Blood Pressure Overview.
